items.name: Hanukkah Salad
ingredients: 1 small white or yellow onion, thinly sliced
1 lb. romaine (about ⅔ head) and/or Little Gem lettuce (4–5 heads)
steps: Preheat oven to 425°. Mix together ½ cup sour cream, 3 Tbsp. drained prepared horseradish, 1 Tbsp. distilled white vinegar, a big pinch of kosher salt, and 1 tsp. water in a small bowl, adding more water a little at a time if needed until dressing it drizzle-able. Taste and season with more salt if needed.
Bake 1 lb. frozen tater tots on a large rimmed baking sheet for half the time of package directions (about 10 minutes).
Meanwhile, place 1 small white or yellow onion, thinly sliced, in a small bowl; pour in cold water to cover and add a few ice cubes. Set onions aside.

Tear pull apart leaves from 1 lb. romaine lettuce (about ⅔ head) and/or Little Gem lettuce (4–5 heads) and tear large leaves in half. Place in a large bowl. Remove tough stems from 1 bunch dill and 1 bunch parsley; discard. Coarsely tear remaining leaves and tender stems. Add to lettuce.

Remove tater tots from oven and, using oven mitts for safety, lay another baking sheet directly on top; firmly press down on tots to flatten. (If you don’t have a second baking sheet, use a heatproof measuring cup or mug instead.) Return tater tots to oven and bake until deep golden brown and crisp, 10–20 minutes.(If your oven has a convection setting, now is a great time to use it.)
Drain reserved onion and pat dry. Thinly slice 2 large apples (about 1 lb.). Add both to bowl with lettuce and herbs.
Drizzle 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil over and add a big pinch of flaky sea salt. Toss to combine, then mound salad on a platter. Evenly scatter tater tots and ¾ cup pomegranate seeds over.
Serve salad with remaining dressing for drizzling over and peeled fresh horseradish (if using) for grating over.

items.name: Turn Your Thanksgiving Leftovers Into Crispy-Topped Turkey Casserole, Tortilla Soup, and More
Mandarin Pomegranate Mocktail
ingredients: 1 ounce sugar-free simple syrup (I love Wholesome Yum)
steps: In a large glass, stir together the pomegranate juice, mandarin juice, lime juice, simple syrup, and orange bitters.
Divide the mixture evenly between two ice-filled glasses. Add one rosemary sprig to each glass, stir, and let sit for a few minutes to infuse.
Top each glass with 1½ ounces sparkling water and serve immediately.

items.name: Suqaar Digaag (Chicken and Vegetable Sauté)
ingredients: 1 lb. (450 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 large yellow onion, halved and sliced
¾ cup (12 g) coarsely chopped cilantro leaves
steps: Toast 1 cup (100 g) whole cumin seeds, 1 cup (70 g) whole coriander seeds, ¼ cup (35 g) black peppercorns, 1 small-to-medium piece of cinnamon bark, 2 Tbsp. green cardamom pods, and 1½ tsp. whole cloves in a medium skillet over medium heat, stirring constantly so the spices don’t burn.
The spices are toasted when they have a slightly darker color and become fragrant, 1–2 minutes. Transfer the toasted spices to a blender or spice grinder and blend until they become a fine powder.
Transfer to a bowl and mix in ¼ cup (30 g) ground turmeric until it’s fully incorporated and the spice mix is golden brown. Allow to cool completely, then store in an airtight container.

In a medium bowl, combine the juice of ½ lemon, 1 tsp. xawaash, 1 tsp. fine sea salt, ½ tsp. paprika, and ⅛ tsp. ground black pepper. Add 1 lb. (450 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces, and mix everything together to coat the chicken. Set aside.

In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil until loose. Add 1 large yellow onion, halved and sliced, and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8 minutes, or until the onion is softened.

Add 6 garlic cloves, minced, and 1 medium jalapeño, halved, and stir for another minute, then add the chicken in a single layer. Allow it to cook undisturbed for 5 minutes, then turn the pieces over and cook for 3 minutes more, until fully cooked through.

Add the remaining 1½ tsp. xawaash, ¾ cup (12 g) coarsely chopped cilantro leaves, 1 medium red bell pepper, sliced, and 1 medium yellow bell pepper, sliced, and stir to combine. Cover the skillet and turn the heat down to medium-low; cook until the peppers have softened, 10 to 15 minutes. Serve hot.

items.name: Excellent Boiled Potatoes
ingredients: ¼ cup Diamond Crystal or 2 Tbsp. plus 2 tsp. Morton kosher salt; plus more
1½ lb. Yukon Gold potatoes (about 3 large or 4 medium)
steps: Combine ¼ cup Diamond Crystal or 2 Tbsp. plus 2 tsp. Morton kosher salt and 10 cups water in a large pot.

Peel 1½ lb. Yukon Gold potatoes (about 3 large or 4 medium). Quarter if potatoes are large, halve if medium, adding to pot as you go. Potatoes should be covered by at least 2" water when finished; add more if needed.
Place pot over high heat and bring water to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until potatoes are cooked through (a fork should slide easily into flesh), 15–20 minutes. Drain in a colander.

Set pot over medium-low heat to cook off any excess water, then add 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter and cook until melted. Stir in 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, and ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper. Remove from heat; mix in ¼ cup finely chopped parsley and 1 tsp. finely grated lemon zest.
Add drained potatoes and toss to coat. Taste and season with more salt if needed. Transfer potatoes to a large shallow bowl to serve.

items.name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Caesar Salad
ingredients: ⅓ cup/80 ml buttermilk or kefir
½ oz./15 g parmesan, finely grated (2 Tbsp.), plus extra to serve
¾ cup/15 g dill, finely chopped, plus a few sprigs to serve
Fine sea salt and black pepper
6 chicken thighs, skin on and bones removed (about 1¾ lb./800 g)
2–3 heads of romaine lettuce, quartered lengthwise (14 oz./400 g)
Handful of croutons, store-bought or homemade, to serve
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.

Whisk together 1 cup/115 g mayonnaise, ⅓ cup/80 ml buttermilk or kefir, 1 tsp. Dijon mustard, 2 green onions, finely chopped, ½ tsp. ground onion, ½ tsp. ground garlic, ½ oz./15 g parmesan, finely grated (2 Tbsp.), and ¾ cup/15 g dill, finely chopped, in a small bowl, along with 1 tsp. fine sea salt and a few grinds of black pepper. Set aside.

Lay 6 chicken thighs, skin on and bones removed (about 1¾ lb./800 g), out flat on a parchment-lined baking sheet and season with ½ tsp. salt and a good grind of pepper. Add 1 lemon, very thinly sliced (about 12 slices), drizzle with 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, and bake for 30–35 minutes, until the chicken is crispy and the lemon slices have started to caramelize.

Transfer the chicken and lemon to a shallow bowl and let rest for 10 minutes. Keep the baking sheet and parchment paper with all the pan juices. Finely chop half the lemon slices and add them to the dressing. Cut the chicken into ½"-/1-cm-thick slices and toss in the bowl with the rest of the lemon slices.

Add 2–3 heads of romaine lettuce, quartered lengthwise (14 oz./400 g), to the baking sheet, season with a pinch of fine sea salt and some black pepper, and turn them a couple of times in the pan juices. Spoon half the dressing over the lettuce and scatter the chicken on top.
Finish with the rest of the dressing, a handful of croutons, store-bought or homemade, the extra parmesan, and a few sprigs of dill.

items.name: Charred Cabbage With Yogurt and Hot Sauce
ingredients: 9 pickled Fresnos, stems removed and roughly chopped, plus 2 Tbsp. brine
¼ preserved lemon, store-bought or homemade, peel only, finely diced
1 cup full-fat Greek yogurt or labne
Fresno Hot Sauce or your favorite hot sauce
steps: In a blender, combine 9 pickled Fresnos, stems removed and roughly chopped, plus 2 Tbsp. brine, 1 small shallot, roughly chopped, 3 garlic cloves, 3 Tbsp. red wine vinegar, juice of 1 navel orange, and 1 tsp. kosher salt. Blend on high, taking a pause to scrape the sides, until smooth.
With the blender running on low, slowly pour in 1 cup extra-virgin olive oil until the sauce is silky and runny. Transfer the sauce to a bottle or jar and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and set racks in the center and top of the oven. Line a sheet tray with parchment paper.

Make the Cabbage: Cut 1 large head green cabbage in half, then slice each half into four wedges. Arrange on the prepared sheet tray, drizzle generously with extra-virgin olive oil and kosher salt, and massage it into all those craggy layers.

Roast on the center rack for 20–25 minutes, until a knife slides through easily. Set the broiler to high and slide the cabbage to the top rack. Broil for 2–4 minutes, until the edges are deeply charred and irresistibly crispy.

While the Cabbage Roasts, Make the Breadcrumbs: In a small skillet over medium heat, melt 1 Tbsp. unsalted butter with 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Stir in ½ cup panko breadcrumbs, 1 garlic clove, finely grated, and ½ tsp. kosher salt, then toast, stirring constantly, until golden and fragrant.
Remove from the heat and mix in ¼ preserved lemon, store-bought or homemade, peel only, finely diced, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh dill, and 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh parsley. Set aside to cool.

Make the Yogurt: In a small bowl, whisk together 1 cup full-fat Greek yogurt or labne, zest and juice ½ lemon, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh dill, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh parsley, and 1 tsp. kosher salt until smooth and creamy.

When the cabbage is ready, swoop the yogurt across a serving plate. Arrange the cabbage wedges at dramatic angles. Drizzle generously with hot sauce, letting it seep into the leaves. Finish with the golden breadcrumbs, fresh dill fronds, and a few extra grates of lemon zest. Serve immediately.

items.name: Homemade Mac and Cheese Recipe
ingredients: ¼ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
steps: Gather and prepare all ingredients.
Cook the macaroni according to the package directions (boil for 7-8 minutes, or until tender). Drain the macaroni in a colander and set aside.
Place the butter and flour in a medium pot over medium heat. Whisk until the butter is melted and the mixture begins to bubble. Once bubbling, continue to whisk and cook for one minute.
After cooking the butter and flour roux, slowly whisk in the milk. I added a few tablespoons at a time, letting each addition thicken before adding more milk.

Cook and whisk over medium heat until the milk gently simmers and thickens to the consistency of heavy cream, about 5 minutes. Be patient and let it fully thicken before adding the cheese, or it won’t melt smoothly.
Once it thickens, turn the burner off. Season the sauce with onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, salt, pepper, and hot sauce. Whisk to combine.

Add the shredded block cheddar a handful at a time, whisking until each addition melts before adding more. If the sauce cools too much, briefly return it to low heat, but don’t let it boil, or it may separate and turn grainy.

Add the cooked and drained pasta to the pot with the cheese sauce and stir to combine. If your pasta appears to be drowning in cheese, don’t worry! It’ll be the perfect consistency as the macaroni absorbs the sauce and thickens up.
Serve hot and enjoy!
Preheat the oven to 350ºF/180C/160C fan or Gas Mark 4.
After combining the drained pasta and cheese sauce, transfer it to a casserole dish.
Top with more shredded cheese, then bake for 15 minutes.
To achieve a golden brown crispy cheese crust, turn on the oven’s broiler for just a few short minutes, watching it closely to prevent burning.

items.name: Spinach Ricotta Ravioli
ingredients: 2 ¼ to 2 ½ cups (300g) “00” soft wheat pasta flour or unbleached all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting the work surface
3 extra large eggs or 3 large eggs + 3 tablespoons water, all at room temperature
⅓ cup freshly grated Parmigiano cheese, plus more for serving
steps: Make a well. Mound the flour onto a clean work surface. Use the back of your hand or the bottom of a bowl to create a wide, shallow well in the mound. The “walls” of the mound should be just high enough to keep the eggs in the well.
Add the eggs. Break the eggs into the flour well and beat lightly, but thoroughly with a fork. Beat in 3 tablespoons of water if you used large, rather than extra large, eggs.

Mix the pasta dough. Use a fork to mix the eggs in a circular motion, slowly incorporating the flour from the inner wall of the well as you mix. When the mixture has thickened to a pasty consistency, begin using your fingers and a bench scraper to incorporate more flour. Continue to mix until a rough, sticky dough has formed.

Knead the pasta dough. Knead the mixture by hand until you have incorporated most, or all of the flour and the dough has a nice, firm, bouncy consistency. Adjust the texture by incorporating more flour or a spritz of water, as needed.
Continue to knead for 5 to 10 minutes, until the dough is smooth, firm, and supple. Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and let it rest at room temperature for 45 to 60 minutes.

Steam the spinach. Wash the spinach and place it in a large skillet or saucepan with the water still clinging to the leaves. Cover and cook over medium-low, turning occasionally, until the spinach is completely wilted and tender, but still a bright, dark green, about 5 to 8 minutes.

Chop the spinach. Transfer the spinach to a colander set in the sink and let sit until cooled enough to handle, then squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Transfer it—now a dense blob of green—to a chopping board and chop finely.

Make the filling. Place the spinach and drained ricotta in a large bowl. Add ⅓ cup freshly grated Parmigiano cheese, the beaten egg, salt, and nutmeg. Mix everything together thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate.

Get ready. Remove the filling from the refrigerator and set up your pasta machine or mixer with the pasta attachment, making sure the pasta roller is at its widest setting (#1 on my hand-crank machine). Sprinkle a little flour on a cleared area around the machine or mixer.
Line two rimmed baking sheets with clean kitchen towels and sprinkle them with flour. This is where you will put your ravioli once you’ve formed them.

Divide the pasta dough. Cut the ball of dough into 4 quarters and rewrap three. Knead the remaining piece briefly on the work surface. With a rolling pin or the heel of your hand, flatten it into a thick oval 3- to 4-inches long.

Roll a dough rectangle. Feed the dough through the pasta machine and then lay it on the work surface. Fold the dough into thirds, as though you were folding a business letter. Sprinkle lightly with flour and pass it through the rollers again. Repeat the folding and rolling process one or two more times to help set the rectangular shape of the dough.

Sheet the pasta. Move the roller setting to the next narrower notch and feed the strip of dough through the setting twice, sprinkling it with a little flour if needed to keep it from sticking. Continue to pass the dough through the rollers twice on each setting until it is about 1/16-inch thick—#5 on my machine. The sheet should just be thin enough to see the shadow of your hand through it.
Add the ravioli filling. Position the strip of pasta on a lightly floured work surface. Mound 1 to 2 teaspoons of filling at 1 ½-inch intervals along the length of the strip, slightly below center.

Seal the ravioli. Dip a finger in water and moisten along the bottom edge of the strip and around each mound of filling. Carefully fold the top of the strip, lengthwise, over the filling so that the top edge meets the bottom edge. Press all around the mounds of filling to squeeze out any air and to seal them.

Cut the ravioli. Use a fluted pasta cutter to cut around each mound to create half-moon or square ravioli. Use a fork to seal them, and set them on one of the towel-lined baking sheets. Make sure the ravioli are not touching, as they might stick together.
Repeat and rest. Repeat this process with the remaining pasta dough. You should end up with 40 to 50 ravioli. Let the ravioli air dry slightly, for about 30 minutes, while you prepare to cook them.
Get ready. Fill a wide high-sided saucepan ½ to ¾ full of water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Warm a serving dish or individual bowls.

Make the Sage Sauce (optional). While the water heats, melt butter and olive oil together in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add sage leaves. Cook, swirling the pan, until the butter browns and smells nutty and sage is lightly browned and crisp, 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Alternatively, warm 2 to 3 cups marinara or your favorite pasta sauce to serving temperature.

Cook the ravioli. Once the water boils, add 1 tablespoon salt and reduce heat to medium-high. The water should not be at a rolling boil, or the ravioli may get tossed around, causing them to tear. Carefully drop ravioli into the pot, cooking them in batches to avoid crowding the pot.
Cook until they are just tender and they float to the surface, for about 5 minutes. Scoop them up, a few at a time, with a large skimmer, taking care to let excess water drain off.

Finish and serve. Place the ravioli in either the warmed serving bowl or in individual bowls and spoon sauce over them. Sprinkle Parmigiano cheese on top, finish with a few crispy sage leaves, and serve.

items.name: 10 Things I’d Buy in the Black Friday Sales 2026 – if I didn’t already have them
Twice Baked Potatoes
ingredients: ¼ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
1¼ cup cheddar cheese shredded and divided, $1.10**
steps: Gather and prepare all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400°F / 200℃ / 180℉ fan. Wash and dry the potatoes well, then use a fork to prick each potato several times.

Place the potatoes on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Drizzle the olive oil over the potatoes, then use your hands or a silicone brush to brush the oil over each potato until it is fully coated. Season the potatoes with ½ teaspoon of salt.
Bake in the preheated oven for 50-60 minutes, or until the potatoes can be pierced easily with a fork. Total baking time will depend on the size of your potatoes.

While the potatoes are baking, chop and cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until brown and crispy, about 10-15 minutes. Remove the cooked bacon from the skillet and allow it to drain on a paper-towel-lined plate.

Once the potatoes are done baking, remove them from the oven and allow them to cool slightly. When the potatoes are cool enough to handle, slice them in half lengthwise. Carefully scoop out the potato flesh, leaving a thin rim of potato (about ¼ inch rim) around the edges to help the skin hold its shape.
Place the scooped-out potato flesh in a large bowl and add the butter, sour cream, milk, salt, and pepper. Use a potato masher or hand mixer to blend the potatoes until light and fluffy.
Add the chopped bacon, half of the sliced green onions, and ½ cup of the shredded cheddar cheese to the mashed potatoes, then fold to combine.
Fill the potato skins with about ⅓ cup of the potato mixture, then sprinkle the remaining cheddar cheese over the top of each potato.

***Bake the potatoes at 400°F in the oven a second time, just until heated through (to the internal temperature of 165°F) and the cheddar cheese is melted on top, about 20 minutes. Top with the remaining green onions and enjoy!
