items.name: Extra-Fluffy Cinnamon Rolls
ingredients: 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt
½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into pieces
½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt
4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, room temperature, plus more for pans
1¼ cups (138 g; or more) powdered sugar
¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt
steps: Whisk ¾ cup whole milk and ¼ cup (31 g) all-purpose flour in a medium saucepan until smooth. Place saucepan over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until mixture is thickened and whisk lines are visible on bottom of pan, about 2 minutes. Scrape tangzhong into the bowl of a stand mixer and let cool.

Add 1 large egg, one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.), ⅓ cup (67 g) granulated sugar, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining 1½ cups whole milk to tangzhong and whisk to combine. Add remaining 5½ cups (688 g) all-purpose flour.

Fit bowl onto stand mixer; fit mixer with dough hook attachment. Mix on low speed until combined, about 1 minute. Increase speed to medium-low and mix, scraping down sides of bowl occasionally, until dough is smooth and elastic, 18–24 minutes.

Pinch off a golf-ball-size piece of dough and stretch between your fingers as thin as possible without breaking. If you can see light through the dough, it’s ready. If not, continue mixing a few more minutes, then try again.

Add ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into pieces, to dough and mix on medium speed until incorporated, about 2 minutes. Continue mixing until dough pulls away cleanly from sides of bowl and is no longer tacky to the touch, 5–7 minutes longer. Remove bowl from mixer and cover with a damp kitchen towel. Let sit in a warm spot until doubled in volume, 60–90 minutes.

While the dough is rising, cook ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until butter foams and milk solids turn dark amber, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a heatproof bowl and let cool slightly. Add 1 cup (packed; 200 g) dark brown sugar, 2 Tbsp.
ground cinnamon, 2 Tbsp. heavy cream, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt to butter and mix to combine.

Butter two 9"-diameter cake pans. Punch down dough and transfer to a lightly floured surface. Stretch dough into a rough rectangle; if dough feels stiff, let sit 5–10 minutes to allow gluten to relax. Arrange dough with short side facing you and roll out to a 24x13" rectangle. Spread filling over dough in an even layer.
Starting at edge closest to you, tightly roll up dough into a log; roll log seam side down. Using a sharp serrated knife and long sawing motions, trim ends of log; discard.

Using serrated knife or, preferably, unflavored dental floss, cut log in half crosswise, then cut each half into 6 equal rounds. (If using dental floss, slide floss underneath dough, then cross over top and pull ends through.) Nestle 6 rounds, cut side down, in each prepared cake pan.
Cover with damp kitchen towels and let sit in a warm spot until doubled in volume, about 30–50 minutes.
Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 350°. Bake rolls until golden on top and puffed (don’t be alarmed if they rise dramatically in the center), 25–30 minutes.

Meanwhile, using an electric mixer on medium speed or a whisk, beat 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, room temperature, and 8 oz. cream cheese, room temperature, in a large bowl, scraping down sides of bowl as needed, until combined. Add 1¼ cups (138 g) powdered sugar, 1 Tbsp. heavy cream, 1 tsp.

lemon zest (if using), and ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt and beat until mixture is smooth and sugar is incorporated. Taste and beat in more powdered sugar (up to ¾ cup) if desired. Thin with more cream as needed, a teaspoonful at a time, until frosting is thick but spreadable.
Let cinnamon rolls cool in pan 5 minutes; spread frosting over.

items.name: 37 Thanksgiving Cocktails and Drinks for Every Guest
Butter Mochi Cake With Maple-Miso Pecans
ingredients: 2 tsp. white or yellow miso (gluten-free if needed)
8 oz. raw pecans, coarsely chopped (about 2 cups)
6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, plus more for pan
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
1 (13.5-oz.) can unsweetened coconut milk, well shaken, heated slightly if fat is solid
2 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
1⅔ cups (254 g) mochiko (sweet rice flour; such as Koda Farms)
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 350°. Lightly oil a rimmed baking sheet with vegetable oil. Whisk 2 Tbsp. pure maple syrup and 2 tsp. white or yellow miso (gluten-free if needed) in a medium bowl until smooth. Add 8 oz. raw pecans, coarsely chopped (about 2 cups) and 1 Tbsp.
sugar and toss until evenly coated. Spread out on prepared baking sheet; bake until fragrant and matte looking, 6–8 minutes (nuts won’t be fully toasted). Let cool.

Lightly grease a 9"-diameter cake pan with unsalted butter and line bottom with a parchment paper round. Vigorously whisk 2 large eggs, 1¼ cups (250 g) sugar, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl until smooth. Add one 13.5-oz.

can unsweetened coconut milk, well shaken, heated slightly if fat is solid, 2 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract, and 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, and whisk well. Add 1⅔ cups (254 g) mochiko and 1 tsp.
baking powder; whisk vigorously until combined and batter is smooth and thick. Scrape batter into prepared pan.

Toss pecans to break up any clumps and scatter evenly over batter, going all the way to the edges (it may seem like a lot). Bake cake until sides start to pull away from pan, top is golden brown, and a tester inserted into the center comes out clean (some pecans will sink), 50–55 minutes.

If pecans begin to brown too quickly, loosely tent pan with foil. Transfer to a wire rack and let cake cool in pan 15 minutes. Turn cake out onto rack; peel away parchment and discard. Carefully turn cake right side up and let cool completely (at least 1 hour).

To serve, slice cake and top with scoops of vanilla ice cream. Do Ahead: Cake can be made 1 day ahead. Store, loosely covered, at room temperature. Editor’s note: This recipe was first published in our August 2023 issue and has been updated with additional guidance. Head this way for more of our favorite pecan recipes →

items.name: Cornbread Salad
ingredients: ½ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
1 green bell pepper medium dice, (1 heaping cup)
15.5 oz. can pinto beans drained and rinsed,
steps: Gather and prepare all ingredients. Preheat your oven to 425°F. Lightly grease a glass loaf pan and set it aside.****
To make the cornbread, in a medium mixing bowl, stir together the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt until evenly combined.
In a separate medium bowl, whisk together the milk, egg, and oil.
Pour the bowl of wet ingredients into the bowl of dry ingredients and whisk just until everything is combined.
Pour the batter into the prepared loaf pan and bake for 20 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown. Set the cornbread aside to cool completely.
To make the ranch, using a medium bowl, combine the mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice, garlic powder, onion powder, parsley, 4 green onions, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine, then set it aside.
Chop the green bell pepper, red onion, and tomatoes into bite-sized pieces and set them aside.

To assemble the salad, cut the cooled cornbread into 1-inch pieces, then add them to the bottom of the trifle dish, covering the bottom. Next, evenly spread the cut green bell peppers on top of the cornbread. Then, layer the drained and rinsed pinto beans, red onions, corn, tomatoes, and cheddar cheese. Make sure each layer is evenly spread.
Lastly, evenly pour over the homemade ranch dressing. Top with the remaining green onions and enjoy!

items.name: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 4 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, divided
1 large yellow onion (about 8 ounces), finely chopped
3 cups white button mushrooms (about 12 ounces), halved or quartered, if large
3 medium carrots, cut into 2 to 3-inch chunks
steps: Get ready. Arrange the wire racks in your oven to accommodate a Dutch oven (with a lid on) in the center. Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Dredge the chicken. Pat the chicken pieces dry and generously season all over with salt and black pepper. Lightly coat both sides with all-purpose flour, tapping each piece to shake off any excess.

Brown the chicken. In a large Dutch oven, or a large, heavy bottomed (oven-safe) skillet with a lid, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium-high. Working in batches if necessary, brown the chicken until golden, about 2 minutes per side. Remove from the pot and set aside.

Sauté the onion and mushrooms. In the same pot, warm the 2 remaining tablespoons of olive oil on medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until golden and slightly browned, about 5 minutes. Then, add the chopped mushrooms in and let them brown and cook down for another 5 minutes.
Add the vegetables. Stir in the garlic, shallots, and carrots, and sauté everything together for a further 2 minutes.

Build the braising liquid. Add one cup of red wine and use a wooden spoon or spatula and rub the bottom of the pan to lift any browned bits into the sauce. Pour in the remaining wine and bring to a simmer for about 10 minutes to evaporate the alcohol and reduce the wine slightly. Pour in the chicken stock, Worcestershire sauce, and thyme. Season with 1 teaspoon salt and mix everything to combine.

Braise the chicken. Place the chicken pieces back into the pot. The chicken should be fully submerged with only small bits poking out of the liquid. Add a little water, if necessary. Cover the Dutch oven or skillet with a lid, and place in the oven to braise for 1 hour.

Reduce the sauce. Remove the chicken pieces from the braising liquid and set them aside. Place the pot on the stove and bring to a simmer on medium high heat. Let the sauce cook down for about 20 to 30 mins, or until the liquid has thickened and reduced by half. Check the sauce periodically until thickened to the texture of cream.

Finish and serve. To serve, fish out the thyme sprigs and return the chicken pieces to the pot. Turn the heat down to medium. Spoon sauce all over the chicken, and let it warm it up again over medium heat for about 2 to 4 minutes. Serve the coq au vin garnished with more fresh thyme.

items.name: Sheet-Pan Cider Vinegar Chicken
ingredients: ½ cup plus 3 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar
1 Tbsp. plus 2 tsp. pure maple syrup
2½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
8 oz. country-style or sourdough bread (about ⅓ loaf), torn into 1" pieces
3 large shallots, quartered lengthwise through root ends
steps: Whisk 5 garlic cloves, finely grated, ½ cup plus 3 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar, 5 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, 3 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, 1 Tbsp. plus 2 tsp. pure maple syrup, 2½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. crushed red pepper flakes (if using) in a measuring glass or small bowl to combine. Transfer 2 Tbsp. vinegar mixture to a small bowl; set aside.

Arrange 3 lb. skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs (6–8), skin side up, on a cutting board. Season lightly with salt. Turn over and season lightly on other side with salt, then carefully use a sharp paring knife to make 3 long slashes, going most of the way through meat (avoid the bone).
Transfer to a large bowl and pour vinegar mixture in measuring glass over. Toss chicken to coat, making sure to get liquid into slashes. Let chicken sit at least 30 minutes and up to 1 hour.
Meanwhile, place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 425°. Place 8 oz. country-style or sourdough bread (about ⅓ loaf), torn into 1" pieces, on a rimmed baking sheet. Drizzle remaining 3 Tbsp.

extra-virgin olive oil over and sprinkle with a pinch of salt and a pinch of freshly ground black pepper; toss to coat. Arrange bread in a single layer and bake until golden, 12–15 minutes. Transfer croutons to a plate; reserve baking sheet.

Arrange reserved chicken on reserved baking sheet and nestle 3 large shallots, quartered lengthwise through root ends, around; pour any excess vinegar mixture in bowl over. Bake chicken until golden, cooked through, and an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest part, avoiding bone, registers at least 165° (it should be well over), 25–30 minutes.

Scatter croutons over empty areas of baking sheet and toss to soak up juices. Roast until chicken and croutons are deeply browned, 10–12 minutes. Let cool 5 minutes, then top with 2 oz. arugula and drizzle with reserved vinegar mixture in small bowl.

items.name: Spinach and Ricotta Puff Pastry Bites
ingredients: 250g / 8 oz frozen chopped spinach , thawed and squeezed of excess water using hands (see FAQ for using fresh spinach)
1 cup tightly packed (100g) shredded cheddar cheese , tasty cheese or other melting cheese you like (not mozzarella, it's not flavoured enough)
½ cup (50g) finely shredded parmesan , shred your own or use store bought (Note 2)
1 garlic clove , minced using a garlic press
½ tsp cooking salt / kosher salt (halve for table salt, +50% for flakes)
2 sheets frozen puff pastry (preferably butter puff pastry) , 25cm/10" squares (180g/6oz per sheet), just barely thawed – Note 3
1 egg yolk , lightly beaten (egg wash) – see here for what I do with egg whites
steps: Mix Filling ingredients. Cut each puff into 9 squares. Spray 18 holes of 2 muffin tins with oil, press puff in. Scoop in filling, bring corners together and press to seal. Lightly brush with egg yolk, bake 25 min at 200°C/390°F (180°C fan) or until deep golden.
Preheat the oven to 200°C/390°F (180°C fan-forced).
Mix Filling – Place the egg, garlic, salt and pepper in a bowl and mix to combine. Then add remaining Filling ingredients and mix until combined. Set aside.
Cut each puff pastry into 9 equal squares (18 in total).

Oil spray muffin tin – Spray 18 holes of two standard muffin tins generously with oil (I use olive oil but any neutral flavoured oil will do). I use all 12 holes on one muffin tin, and 6 holes on the other.
Lightly press the puff pastry squares into the muffin tin holes.
Fill – Divide the Filling between the holes (I use a size 30 cookie scoop which is just about perfect to use up all the filling!).

Enclose – Bring the four corners into the centre and press together to seal, stretching and pinching the pastry as needed. Don't completely enclose the filling – you want some spinach peeking through between the folds to create a pretty flower pattern.
And don't overfill or the corners won't seal properly and the pastries may burst open during baking. (Note: I don't seal with egg wash – see Note 4 for why)

Lightly brush the top of the puff pastry with egg yolk – not down the side, and don't be too generous as it will drip down the side and make the puff pastry stick to the muffin in (remember, egg is an excellent food glue!).

Bake – Put the full muffin tin on the top shelf and the partially filled muffin tin on the shelf underneath. Bake for 25 minutes or until deep golden and crispy (the partially filled muffin tin might need an extra 5 minutes).
Serve – Allow to rest for 5 minutes before removing the puffs from the holes. Serve warm if you can, though they are still really nice at room temperature!

To freeze or refrigerate – Following recipe until you have filled and sealed the puffs, but do not brush with yolk. (Note 5) Remove puffs from muffin tin then refrigerate (up to 2 days) or freeze in an airtight container until required. If the puff is too soft to pick up without deforming, refrigerate in the muffin tin for 30 minutes to firm up, then remove.

Baking – Preheat the oven to 190°C/375°F (170°C fan-forced), line a large baking tray with paper. Place puffs on (do not thaw frozen ones), brush with egg yolk. Bake refrigerated puffs for 30 minutes, and frozen puffs for 35 – 40 minutes, or until deep golden and crispy.

Note: They come out about 15% flatter because we're not using a muffin tin which to me is a small trade off for the convenience of not having to wash two oily muffin tins. But if you want puffy parcels like pictured, bake them in a muffin tin.

items.name: Pecan Pie Bars
ingredients: 1 cup plus 5 tablespoons (10.5 ounces or 300 grams) unsalted butter (to be used for crust and pecan layer)
2 cups plus 2 tablespoons (275 grams) all-purpose flour
½ cup (60 to 100 grams) granulated or powdered sugar
1 teaspoon kosher salt (Diamond brand; use half of others)
⅔ cups (140 grams) packed dark brown sugar
½ teaspoon flaky or coarse sea salt, plus an extra pinch or two to finish
1 teaspoon vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
3 ¼ cups (12 ounces or 340 grams) pecan halves, lightly toasted
1 cup (6 ounces or 170 grams) chocolate chips, semisweet or bittersweet are great here
steps: Heat oven: To 350°F (175°C). Use a large sheet of parchment paper to line the bottom and sides of a 9×13-inch pan, pressing it into the corners and up the sides. This will make it very easy to remove the bars.
[If your pecans aren’t already toasted, while the oven heats, place them on a sheet pan and bake them for 8 to 10 minutes, until fragrant. Set aside until needed.]

Brown the butter: In a medium-large saucepan (we’ll use this as the bowl to mix the pecan layer in a bit), melt butter over medium-high heat. It will melt, then foam, then begin to developed fragrant, toasted brown specks at the edges of the pan.

Remove from heat when you see it starting to brown; the residual heat will be sufficient to toast the rest of the butter to a medium brown color. Carefully, so it doesn’t splatter, add 2 tablespoons of water.

Make the shortbread crust: In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, and salt. Measure 1 cup of the browned butter (leaving the rest in the saucepan) and add it to the flour mixture, stirring it until it’s mixed into a soft, crumbly dough.

Scatter the dough over your prepared pan and press it evenly across the bottom and ¼-inch further up at the edges. Transfer to the oven and bake for 15 to 17 minutes, until it smells fragrant and begins to get more golden at the edges.

Meanwhile, make the pecan layer: Add brown sugar, honey, heavy cream, flaky salt, cider vinegar, and vanilla to the remaining brown butter in your saucepan and whisk to combine. Add eggs, one at a time, whisking until fully mixed. Add your toasted pecan halves (still a little warm is fine) and stir to coat with honey mixture. Stir in chocolate chips last.

Assemble and bake: Pour the pecan mixture over the crust — it’s fine if it’s still hot from the oven — then sprinkle a few flakes of salt over the top. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the edges are set but the center is somewhat firm to the touch, but still has some jiggle to it.

Transfer pan to a cooling rack and let the bars cool completely. You can hurry this along in the fridge. Use the edges of the parchment paper to lift bars out and onto a cutting board. Cut into your desired size pieces.
Do ahead: These bars keep in the fridge for up to a week, but only if you hide them from family and, sometimes, yourself.

items.name: BA's Best Lasagna
ingredients: Kosher salt, freshly ground black pepper
2 oz. pancetta (Italian bacon) or slab bacon, chopped
¼ cup plus 3 Tbsp. all-purpose flour
4 oz. Parmesan cheese, coarsely grated (about 1 cup)
1¼ lb. dried lasagna noodles (preferably De Cecco)
steps: Preheat oven to 225°. Mix 2 lb. ground pork and 1 lb. ground beef chuck (20% fat) with your hands in a large bowl; season generously with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, then mix again. Form into about 18 large meatballs (they don’t need to be perfect—you’ll be mashing them later).

Warm 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high heat. Working in 2 batches, cook meatballs, turning occasionally and reducing heat if bottom of pot looks in danger of scorching, until browned all over, about 6 minutes per batch. Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet as they’re done.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 2 oz. pancetta (Italian bacon) or slab bacon, chopped, to pot and cook, stirring often, until lightly browned and beginning to crisp, about 5 minutes.

Add 1 medium onion, finely chopped, 1 celery stalk, finely chopped, 1 medium carrot, peeled, finely chopped, and 6 garlic cloves, sliced, and cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are softened, 6–8 minutes. Add 2 Tbsp.
tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, until paste is darkened in color, about 2 minutes.

Add ¾ cup dry white wine and cook, stirring occasionally, until almost completely evaporated, about 5 minutes. Add one 28-oz. can whole peeled tomatoes, crushing with your hands, and increase heat to medium-high.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until liquid is jammy and reduced by about half, 8–10 minutes. Add 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth and 1 cup whole milk, then return meatballs to pot. Bring to a simmer.

Cover pot partially with a lid, transfer to oven, and cook, checking every hour or so to ensure liquid is at a low simmer and adjusting oven temperature as needed, until meatballs are falling-apart tender, 3–4 hours.

Using a potato masher, break meatballs apart and incorporate into liquid (you should have about 8 cups ragù; transfer pot to stovetop and simmer gently to reduce if needed). Taste and season with more salt and black pepper if needed. Do ahead: Ragù can be made 4 days ahead. Let cool; cover and chill, or freeze up to 3 months.

Melt 7 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in ¼ cup plus 3 Tbsp. all-purpose flour and cook, whisking occasionally, until mixture smells slightly nutty, about 4 minutes. Whisking constantly, add 6 cups whole milk.
Increase heat to medium-high and continue whisking until mixture comes to a simmer. Reduce heat to maintain a simmer and cook, whisking occasionally, until béchamel thickens, about 4 minutes.

Continue cooking, whisking occasionally and adjusting heat as needed to maintain a gentle simmer, until béchamel is smooth and velvety, 8–10 minutes more. Remove from heat and whisk in 4 oz. Parmesan cheese, coarsely grated (about 1 cup), a pinch of cayenne pepper, and a pinch of ground nutmeg.
(You should have about 6 cups béchamel.) Season with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper. Transfer to a large bowl and press plastic wrap directly onto surface; let cool slightly.

Preheat oven to 325°. Note: You can skip the following boiling step (and save yourself a pot to wash!). In side-by-side retests, the BA Test Kitchen found that regular dried lasagna noodles (not no-boil) produced similar results whether parboiled or layered straight from the box.

To use them uncooked, spread the ragù and béchamel all the way to the edges, covering every noodle completely, and make sure the sauce blankets the top layer of noodles before baking. If parboiling: Cook 1¼ lb.

dried lasagna noodles in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally and separating them so they don’t stick together, until just starting to soften but still snap in half rather than bend when folded; 3 minutes is the magic number.

The noodles will be so firm it will just seem all wrong. Using tongs, transfer noodles to a large bowl of cold water to cool. Drain and lay flat in a single layer on a rimmed baking sheet, separated by parchment or wax paper.

Lightly coat a 13x9", 4–6-qt. glass or ceramic baking dish with extra-virgin olive oil. Spread 1½ cups ragù in dish. Lay a single layer of noodles over ragù (cut or break noodles as needed to fill any gaps).

Spoon 1¼ cups béchamel over noodles, spreading in an even layer with a small offset spatula. Top béchamel with 1½ cups of meat sauce. Repeat layering noodles, béchamel, and ragù 3 more times. Top with a fifth layer of noodles and the remaining 1 cup béchamel.

Note: For more pasta in every bite, build six layers instead of five. Start with the same 1½ cups ragù on the bottom of the dish, but use 1 cup béchamel and 1¼ cups ragù between the pasta layers. Finish with a sixth layer of pasta and the remaining 1 cup béchamel.

Cover with a lightly oiled piece of aluminum foil and set lasagna pan on a rimmed baking sheet (just to catch drips). Bake lasagna until bubbling gently around the edges, about 1 hour. Remove from oven. Increase oven temperature to 425° and carefully place rack in top of oven.

Remove foil from lasagna and continue to bake until top is browned and crisp around the edges, 10–15 minutes longer. Let sit 10 minutes before serving. Do ahead: Béchamel can be made 1 day ahead; keep chilled. Rewarm just enough to loosen before using.
Lasagna can be assembled 1 month ahead; let cool, then cover with plastic and freeze. Let frozen lasagna thaw overnight in fridge before baking.
Editor’s note: This recipe first appeared in our February 2018 issue as part of BA’s Best, our vault of the Test Kitchen’s definitive takes on iconic dishes.

It has been updated with clearer assembly instructions and guidance from additional BA Test Kitchen testing, including the option to skip parboiling regular dried lasagna noodles. Head this way for more of our comfort food favorites →

items.name: 11 Leftover Turkey Sandwiches to Look Forward To
How to Make Whipped Cream Perfectly, Every Time
Maple-Sausage Breakfast Casserole
ingredients: 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
2 lb. breakfast sausage, casings removed if needed
8 oz. sharp yellow cheddar, coarsely grated (about 2 cups)
2 Tbsp. pure maple syrup, plus more for serving
2 Tbsp. unsalted butter, plus more for serving
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 400°. Lightly coat a 13x9" baking dish with nonstick vegetable oil spray. Whisk 2½ cups (313 g) all-purpose flour, ¼ cup (50 g) sugar, 2 Tbsp. baking powder, 2 tsp. freshly ground pepper, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl to combine. Set aside.

Cook 2 lb. breakfast sausage, casings removed if needed, in a large skillet set over medium-high heat, stirring and breaking into small pieces with a wooden spoon, until browned and cooked through, 10–12 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer sausage to a small plate, leaving fat behind.

Pour fat into a heatproof measuring glass. You want ½ cup fat; spoon out any excess or pour in vegetable oil as needed if you don’t have enough. Stir 2 large eggs and 2 cups whole milk into fat. Let sausage cool slightly, then crumble into small, even pieces with your hands.

Pour fat mixture into reserved dry ingredients and stir until just combined and no large dry pockets of flour remain (batter may be thin and lumpy; it’ll be fine). Set aside ½ cup sausage and ½ cup cheese from 8 oz. sharp yellow cheddar, coarsely grated (about 2 cups), for topping, then add remaining sausage and cheddar to batter and stirring until evenly distributed.

Scrape batter into prepared baking dish and evenly scatter reserved sausage and cheese over. Bake casserole until top springs back when gently pressed with your finger and a tester inserted into the center comes out with just a few moist crumbs attached, 20–30 minutes.
Just before casserole is done, heat 2 Tbsp. pure maple syrup and 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a small skillet over medium, stirring occasionally, until butter is melted, about 2 minutes.
Brush maple butter over casserole and let cool 10 minutes. Cut into squares. Serve with more maple syrup and butter alongside.

items.name: Leftover Turkey Casserole
ingredients: 2 ounces whole wheat butter crackers (about 20 total, coarsely crumbled (about 1 heaping cup))
¾ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (divided)
1 ¼ cups turkey stock (unsalted or low-sodium)
1 teaspoon kosher salt (plus additional to taste)
½ cup low-fat cottage cheese (about 4 ounces)
4 ounces low-fat cream cheese (cut into 4 cubes)
8 ounces cooked turkey breast (shredded or chopped, about 2 cups)
12 ounces leftover roasted vegetables (about 3 cups such as green beans, or broccoli (roughly chopped))
2 scallions (about 1 ounce, thinly sliced, divided (about ⅓ cup))
steps: Arrange a rack in the lower third of the oven and preheat to 375°F. Spray a 2-quart baking dish with olive oil and set aside.

Put the crumbled crackers into a medium bowl, spray generously with olive oil, and stir to coat. Sprinkle with ½ teaspoon garlic powder, ½ teaspoon onion powder, and ¼ teaspoon black pepper and stir again to coat in the spices. Set aside.
In a large high-sided skillet, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute. Gradually add the turkey stock while whisking constantly to prevent lumps.

Whisk in the salt and the remaining 1 ¼ teaspoons garlic powder, 1 ¼ teaspoons onion powder, and ½ teaspoon black pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook, whisking constantly, until thickened to the consistency of a creamy gravy, 3 to 5 minutes.

Reduce the heat to low, add the cottage cheese and cream cheese, and stir until the cream cheese has melted into the gravy, about 1 minute. Add the shredded turkey, roasted vegetables, and half of the sliced scallions and stir to combine.
Taste and season the turkey mixture with more salt if needed. Spoon the mixture into the prepared baking dish pressing down to spread, then sprinkle evenly with the cracker topping.

Bake until the edges are bubbling and the cracker topping is slightly more browned in spots and crispy, 20 to 25 minutes. Remove from the oven and rest 5 minutes. Sprinkle the top with the remaining sliced scallions and serve.

items.name: Red-Wine-Braised Short Ribs
ingredients: 5 lb. English-style bone-in beef short ribs, cut crosswise into 2" pieces by your butcher
Kosher salt, freshly ground black pepper
1 (750-ml) bottle dry red wine (preferably Cabernet Sauvignon)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°. Season 5 lb. bone-in beef short ribs, cut crosswise into 2" pieces by your butcher, with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper. Heat 3 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high.
Working in 2 batches, cook short ribs, turning occasionally, until browned on all sides, about 8 minutes per batch. Transfer to a plate. Pour off all but 3 Tbsp. drippings from pot.

Cook 3 medium onions, chopped, 3 medium carrots, peeled, chopped, and 2 celery stalks, chopped, in same pot over medium-high heat, stirring often, until onions are browned, about 5 minutes. Add 3 Tbsp. all-purpose flour and 1 Tbsp. tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, until combined and deep red, 2–3 minutes.

Stir in one 750-ml bottle dry red wine (preferably Cabernet Sauvignon), then add short ribs along with any juices that have accumulated on the plate. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium and simmer until wine is reduced by half, about 25 minutes.

Add 1 head of garlic, halved crosswise, 10 sprigs parsley, 8 sprigs thyme, 4 sprigs oregano, 2 sprigs rosemary, and 2 fresh or dried bay leaves; stir in 4 cups low-sodium beef broth. Bring to a boil, cover, and transfer pot to oven. Braise until short ribs are tender, 2–2½ hours.

Uncover pot and transfer short ribs to a platter. Strain sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a heatproof measuring glass; spoon fat from surface and discard. Season sauce with salt and pepper. Arrange ribs in shallow bowls, over mashed potatoes if desired, and spoon sauce over.
Editor’s note: This short ribs recipe was first printed in our October 2011 issue; head this way for more of our favorite comfort foods →

items.name: Chicken and Stuffing Casserole
ingredients: 6 oz. box chicken flavored stuffing mix
steps: Gather and prepare all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9×9-inch casserole dish with nonstick cooking spray; set aside.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels and season evenly with ½ teaspoon of salt and ½ teaspoon of pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the cubed chicken in an even layer. Sear in batches if needed.
Cook undisturbed for 3 minutes, then flip, and cook for another 3 minutes. Remove the chicken from the skillet and place it on paper towels to drain. Set aside.
Turn the heat to medium and melt 4 Tbsp of butter in the skillet, then sprinkle in the flour and cook for about 2 minutes, whisking constantly.
Slowly whisk in 1 cup of chicken broth, whisk until it thickens, for about 3 minutes.
Next, whisk in the milk, remaining salt and pepper, onion powder, and garlic powder. Keep whisking until thick, for about 3 minutes. Turn off the heat and set aside.
Layer the cooked chicken on the bottom of the casserole dish in an even layer.
Spoon the sauce and spread evenly over the chicken.
Then top the casserole evenly with the stuffing mix. Pour the remaining 1 cup of chicken broth evenly over the stuffing. Dice the remaining butter into small cubes and dot on top of the stuffing.
Bake the casserole, uncovered, in the oven for about 30 minutes until golden brown. Let it cool for 10 minutes before serving.

items.name: 11 Pasta Sauce Recipes for Easy, Cozy Dinners
Caramelized Cabbage Pasta
ingredients: 1 large head of green cabbage (about 3 lb.), cored, thinly sliced
steps: Cook 12 oz. spaghetti in a large pot of boiling generously salted water, stirring occasionally, until very al dente, about 1 minute less than package directions. Drain, reserving 2 cups pasta cooking liquid. Set aside.

Melt 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter in same pot over high heat. Add 1 large head of green cabbage (about 3 lb.), cored, thinly sliced, and 6 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and cook, stirring often, until cabbage is very tender and browned in spots, 18–25 minutes.

Add zest of 1 lemon, 2 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about 1 cup), 1½ cups heavy cream, 2 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, and reserved pasta to cabbage and toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add pasta cooking liquid a splash at a time, tossing constantly, until glossy. Taste pasta and season with kosher salt and freshly ground pepper.
Divide pasta among shallow bowls and top with finely chopped dill if desired.

items.name: Mulled Wine
ingredients: 750 ml (1 bottled) Merlot or other smooth, full-bodied red wine , use a decent drinking one (Note 1)
1 large orange (we need the peel from ½ the orange + ½ cup juice)
3 cardamom pods , lightly crushed to burst open using a meat mallet or rolling pin
½ cup (tightly packed) brown sugar , or more as desired (I don’t like my mulled wine soda-sweet)
steps: Soak raisins in brandy for 2 hrs+. Strain into saucepan, add all Mulled Wine ingredients. Simmer 5 min, put lid on, turn off stove and steep 1 hr. Scoop out spices and orange, rewarm, put raisins and almonds into mug, ladle in mulled wine.
Soak raisins 2 hours – Put the raisins and brandy in a glass. Set aside for 2 hours+ to let the raisins plump up (even overnight is fine).

Mulled wine mixture – Strain the brandy into a large saucepan. Set the raisins aside for serving. Add remaining Mulled Wine ingredients into the saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium high heat then let it simmer gently on medium for 5 minutes.

Steep 1 hour – Put a lid on then turn off the stove and let everything steep for 1 hour. This lets all the flavour of the spices and orange peel gently infuse into the wine rather than using a long simmer which cooks off the alcohol (it's Christmas! Let me have my booze!)
Rewarm – Scoop the spices and orange peel out using a slotting spoon. Turn the stove on to re-warm the wine.
Serve – Put a spoonful of boozy raisins and slivered almonds into a mug or glass (if using). Ladle in warm mulled wine. Optional – garnish by adding a small slice of orange and cinnamon stick. Enjoy!

items.name: 31 Cranberry Recipes for Thanksgiving and Beyond
Maple-Glazed Carrots
ingredients: 2 lb. medium carrots, tops trimmed to about ½", scrubbed
6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into pieces
⅓ cup (packed; 70 g) light brown sugar
¾ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes
steps: Place rack in middle of oven and preheat oven to 400°. Line a rimmed baking sheet with 3 sheets of foil (you’ll need it!). Cut 2 lb. medium carrots, tops trimmed to about ½", scrubbed, on a diagonal into 3" pieces (halved or quartered lengthwise if large).

Spread out carrots on foil. Evenly top with 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into pieces, ⅓ cup (packed; 70 g) light brown sugar, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, and ¾ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes. Season with kosher salt and toss to combine.

Roast carrots, tossing every 20 minutes, until tender and browned around the edges, 50–60 minutes. Watch closely as the carrots begin to brown; the glaze can darken quickly. Transfer to a platter and drizzle with any remaining syrup. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt (if using).
Editor’s note: This recipe for maple carrots was first published in November 2018; it has been updated for clarity and style. Head this way for more of our best carrot recipes →

items.name: BA's Best Pecan Pie
ingredients: 1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt
2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for surface
5 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, cut into pieces
3 Tbsp. chilled lard or vegetable shortening
4 large eggs, room temperature, beaten to blend
⅔ cup (packed; 134 g) light brown sugar
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled
steps: Pulse 1 Tbsp. sugar, 1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 2 cups all-purpose flour in a food processor until combined. Add 5 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, cut into pieces, and 3 Tbsp.

chilled lard or vegetable shortening and pulse until mixture resembles coarse meal with a few pieces of butter and lard visible, about fifteen 1-second pulses. With motor running, drizzle in 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar and 5½ Tbsp.
ice water and pulse until dough is still crumbly but just holds together when squeezed (add 1 tsp. water at a time if necessary, but be careful not to overwork dough).
Turn out dough onto a work surface. Knead 1–2 times, pressing just to incorporate any shaggy pieces. Flatten into a 6"-wide disk. Wrap with plastic wrap and chill at least 1 hour.

Preheat oven to 425°. Roll out dough on a lightly floured work surface to a 14" round. Transfer to a 9" pie pan. Pick up edges and allow dough to slump down into dish, letting excess dough hang over dish. Trim, leaving about a 1" overhang. Fold overhang under; pinch and crimp. Chill 30 minutes.

Line dough with parchment paper or foil, leaving some overhang. Fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake until crust is dry around the edges and just beginning to lightly brown, 25–35 minutes. Carefully remove parchment and weights and reduce oven temperature to 350°.

Bake until crust is set and beginning to brown in the center, 10–15 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack and let cool. Do Ahead: Dough can be made 3 days ahead; keep chilled, or freeze up to 2 months. Crust can be baked 1 day ahead; tightly wrap and store at room temperature.
Preheat oven to 350°. Toast 2 cups (225 g) pecan halves on a rimmed baking sheet until browned and fragrant, 8–10 minutes. Let cool.

Reduce oven temperature to 325°. Whisk 4 large eggs, room temperature, beaten to blend, 1 cup light corn syrup, ⅔ cup (packed; 134 g) light brown sugar, 1 Tbsp. robust-flavored (dark) molasses, 1 Tbsp. vanilla extract, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp.
Morton kosher salt in a large bowl until smooth. Slowly whisk in 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, until combined. Fold in pecans and pour into cooled crust.

Bake pie until edges are set and slightly puffed but center is recessed and wobbles like Jell-O, 55–70 minutes (it will continue to set after baking). Transfer to a wire rack and let cool at least 3 hours before slicing. Serve with vanilla ice cream.

Do Ahead: Pie can be baked 1 day ahead; tightly wrap and chill. Serve warm or at room temperature. Editor’s note: This pecan pie recipe was first published in November 2016 and has been updated for style. For more of our best pie recipes, head this way →

items.name: How to Blind-Bake Pie Crust—and When You Need To
Charcuterie Baked Brie
ingredients: ⅓ cup fig jam or jam of choice
1 clove garlic grated or very finely minced
⅛ teaspoon red pepper flakes optional
steps: Place a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 375°F.
With the tip of a sharp knife, score the Brie horizontally, then vertically to create a grid pattern. Arrange in the center of a small baking dish.
In a small bowl, combine the jam, garlic, rosemary, and red pepper flakes. Microwave for 30 seconds so the jam thins out a bit.
Stuff prosciutto into the score marks in the Brie so bits of it poke out all over. Pour the jam mixture all over the top.
Arrange baguette slices around the Brie so the cut sides are exposed and can toast in the oven. Drizzle the slices with olive oil.
Bake the Brie until hot and turning melty and the slices are crisp (they won't turn very golden but will be toasty), about 20 minutes. Enjoy warm.

items.name: Thanksgiving Turkey Recipe
ingredients: 12-14 lbs. whole turkey with giblets, (mine was 13.72lbs) $11.52*
1 Tbsp + 1 tsp Morton’s Kosher Salt see important salt notes below!! $0.05**
2 sticks unsalted butter room temperature, (1 cup)
4 garlic cloves pressed or finely minced, (about 1 Tbsp)
steps: Safely Thaw (3 to 4 Days Ahead): Make sure to start defrosting your whole turkey in the refrigerator, unopened, on a rimmed tray at least 3 to 4 full days before the day you plan to eat it. Start thawing on Sunday or Monday morning if you plan to dry-brine on Wednesday.

Unwrap & Trim: Once thawed, unwrap the turkey and remove the neck and giblets from the cavities. Using kitchen shears, trim away the excess neck skin and tail fat. Pour out any pooled juices from the cavity.

Pat Bone-Dry: Thoroughly dab the entire turkey inside and out with clean paper towels until completely dry. You should also dab underneath the skin of the turkey dry; the space between the breast meat and the skin. Transfer the bird to a wire rack set inside your large baking sheet or roasting pan.
Tuck the turkey’s wings behind it’s back in preparation for when it goes in the oven (this keeps the wings from burning!).

(If you're planning to dry brine your turkey, read on. If you are skipping the dry brine, go to Step 6!) Apply the Dry Brine: Measure out 1 Tbsp + 1 tsp of Morton’s Kosher Salt (using Morton's ensures accurate salinity). Rub ½ tsp inside the cavity, ½ tsp under the breast skin directly onto the meat, and the remaining salt evenly over the exterior skin.

Air-Chill Uncovered (optional, if dry brining): Make sure the skin is covering the breast meat again and place the bird back in your refrigerator uncovered for 12-24 hours (overnight is ideal). This dehydrates the outer skin so it bakes up nice and crisp.
Mix Compound Butter: Combine the room temperature/softened unsalted butter, pressed garlic, black pepper, rosemary, thyme, sage, and paprika in a bowl using a fork until mostly smooth.
Mix Seasoning Oil: In a small cup, stir together the canola oil, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and ground mustard to create your "seasoning salt" exterior paste.

Apply Compound Butter Under the Skin: Take the turkey out 30 minutes before roasting to take the chill off. Gently slide your fingers under the breast and thigh skin to loosen pockets. Divide your compound butter in half, pushing half deep under the left breast/thigh and half under the right.
Then, massage gently through the skin with clean, dry hands from the outside (on top of the skin) to distribute.

Brush Exterior with Oil: Using a pastry brush, gently apply a micro-thin sheen of the seasoning oil mixture all over the outside skin (drumsticks, wings, and exterior). Dab gently over the buttered areas so you don't displace the butter.

Insert the probe thermometer into the thickest part of the turkey breast that will be facing the oven door. This way, the cable will be closest to the door and the screen showing you the temperature can neatly rest on a countertop. I highly recommend you use a probe thermometer to avoid a dry turkey breast!

Roast to Perfection: Roast your unstuffed bird at 350°F for roughly 2-2 ½ hours for a sheet pan with wire rack, or 2½-3 hours if using a high-sided roasting pan. Pull the bird when an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the breast reads 157°F-160°F.

The breast will hit 165°F via carryover heat while resting on the counter, rather than needing to hit 165°F inside the oven. Let the turkey rest uncovered for 30-45 minutes before carving to let internal juices settle as carryover heat finishes bringing it to temperature.

items.name: Caldo Verde
ingredients: 4 ounces chouriço, linguiça, or dry-cured Spanish chorizo (113g), sliced ¼-inch thick
1 ½ pounds Yukon Gold potatoes (680g), peeled and cubed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 pound kale or collard greens (454g), stems removed
steps: Fry the chorizo. Set a large pot over medium heat. Add the olive oil. Once the olive oil shimmers, add the sliced chorizo in a single layer. Fry until the fat is rendered and the chorizo begins to brown, about 2 minutes per side. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the chorizo to a plate, leaving the drippings in the pot. Set aside until serving.
Cook the aromatics. Add the onions to the pot and sauté until soft and translucent, 10 minutes. Add the garlic, and cook until fragrant, 1 minute.
Boil the potatoes. Add the water, potatoes, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer, uncovered, for 20 to 25 minutes until the potatoes are very soft.

Prepare the greens. While the potatoes simmer, chiffonade the kale. Stack several kale leaves and roll them lengthwise into a tight cylinder. Cut crosswise into thin slices, 1/16 to ⅛ inch wide. Then cut the strips into 1-inch lengths. Repeat with the remaining kale.
Purée the soup. Once the potatoes are tender, remove the pot from the heat. Use an immersion blender to purée the soup.
Cook the greens. Return the pot to medium heat and bring it back to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, stir in the greens, and simmer, uncovered, until the greens are tender, 5 to 10 minutes.
Finish and serve. Stir in the vinegar, taste, and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper. To serve, ladle into bowls and top with a few slices of chorizo.

items.name: Ham and Potato Soup
ingredients: 1 cup low-fat or full-fat Greek yogurt plus additional for serving (do not use fat free, as it may curdle)
½ teaspoon kosher salt plus additional to taste
3 cups diced cooked ham about 1 pound
6 ounces sharp cheddar cheese shredded, plus additional for serving
steps: In a large Dutch oven or similar large, sturdy pot, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring periodically, until it’s completely soft and turning golden, about 20 minutes. Adjust the heat as needed so it doesn't turn dark brown or crisp. This step is key to developing the flavors in the soup, so don't shortcut it.
Place the Greek yogurt in a medium bowl and let come to room temperature.
While the onion cooks, prep the vegetables: Scrub and peel the carrots, then cut into ¼-inch dice. Dice the celery. Mince the garlic. Scrub and peel the potatoes, then cut into ¾-inch cubes.

Once the onions are fully softened, increase the heat to medium and add the carrots and celery. Cook 5 minutes, stirring every minute or so. Stir in the garlic, salt, black pepper, and cayenne and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 full minute. No dry bits of flour should remain, and the mixture will seem dry and thick.
Add the broth about a cup at a time, stirring after each addition until smooth before adding the next.

Add the potatoes and ham. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork, 12 to 15 minutes. Stir once or twice throughout, running a spoon along the bottom to prevent sticking.
Reduce the heat to low. Stir in the evaporated milk and let it warm through for 2 minutes.

With a potato masher, lightly mash the soup a few times to thicken it further (you still want plenty of texture). Stir in the cheddar a handful at a time, stirring until each addition melts before adding the next.

Turn off the heat. Scoop a ladle of the hot soup into the bowl with the Greek yogurt and stir to combine. Then, scrape the mixture back into the pot and stir it all together (this prevents the yogurt from curdling).
Taste and add salt and pepper as needed (the seasoning will depend upon the saltiness of your ham). Serve hot, topped with extra cheddar, a spoonful of Greek yogurt, and green onions.

items.name: Herby Sheet-Pan Meatballs With Feta
ingredients: ½ cup finely chopped dill and/or parsley; plus more for serving (optional)
2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, plus more
1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for hands
1 large red onion, cut through root end into 2"-thick wedges
Sliced cucumbers and crumbled feta (optional), country-style bread, and lemon wedges (for serving)
steps: Place a rack in bottom third of oven; preheat to 425°. Using a sturdy wooden spoon, vigorously mix 2 large eggs, zest of 1 lemon, 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, 1 cup panko, ½ cup finely chopped dill and/or parsley, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 2 tsp. dried oregano, 1 tsp.

freshly ground pepper, 1 tsp. ground cumin, and ½ cup water in a large bowl until nearly a smooth paste. Add 1 lb. ground beef and mix vigorously until well combined and mixture is slightly tacky. Oil your hands; divide mixture into 16 portions and roll into balls.
Arrange on a large rimmed baking sheet.

Toss 1 large red onion, cut through root end into 2"-thick wedges, 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, a large pinch of salt, and a large pinch of pepper in a small bowl. Arrange in a single layer around meatballs. Bake meatballs and onions until meatballs are deeply browned underneath and an instant-read thermometer inserted into centers registers 160°, 25–30 minutes. Let cool slightly.
To serve, generously top with sliced cucumbers, crumbled feta, and more dill and/or parsley if desired. Serve with country-style bread and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

items.name: Kale Pesto Pasta
ingredients: 4 cups tightly packed (100g) kale leaves , torn by hand, about 4 stems (curly kale or Cavolo nero/lacinto) – Note 1
½ cup tightly packed (50g) finely grated parmesan , store bought sandy-type from fridge is fine here, else grate your own – Note 2
1 garlic clove , minced using garlic press
½ cup (50g) walnuts – substitute cashews or almonds, or halve the quantity for pine nuts
½ cup (125 ml) extra virgin olive oil
¾ tsp cooking salt / kosher salt
½ tsp red pepper flakes , for slight warmth – feel free to reduce, or omit (substitute with black pepper)
500g / 1 lb pasta of choice – long or short (pictured: Casarecce N.88)
2 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt , for pasta cooking water
⅓ cup reserved pasta cooking water , for pasta tossing
steps: Toast walnuts, pour into bowl with all pesto ingredients, blitz until finely puréed. Toss with hot pasta and with ⅓ cup pasta cooking water.
Cook pasta – Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the 2 teaspoons of salt. Add the pasta and cook for the time per the packet directions.
Reserve water – Just before draining, scoop out 1 cup of pasta cooking water. Then drain the pasta and return into the pasta cooking pot.
Toast walnuts – Heat a small pan over medium high heat (no oil). Add the walnuts and toast for 3 minutes, tossing every now and then, until it has light brown spots and it smells nutty.

Blitz pesto – Immediately pour the walnuts into a large bowl (no need to cool, can blitz while hot). Add remaining pesto ingredients. Blitz using a stick blender until the kale is as finely blitzed as you can, about 20 – 30 seconds. It won't turn into a smoothie (kale is hardy!). (Note 3 on food processor)

Toss with pasta – Pour over the hot pasta and add ⅓ cup of the reserved pasta cooking water. Toss well until evenly coated, using extra pasta cooking water as needed to loosen, then serve immediately garnished with extra parmesan. It's especially nice hot (brings out the garlic and parmesan flavour) though also lovely served as a cold pasta salad.

items.name: 7 Day High Protein Diet Meal Plan
Easy Homemade Cornbread Recipe
steps: Gather and measure all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 425ºF/220℃/200℃ fan or Gas Mark 7 and coat the inside of a 9-inch pie plate, cast iron skillet, or 8×8 casserole dish with non-stick spray (or butter for more flavor).
In a large bowl, stir together the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the milk, egg, and oil.
Pour the bowl of wet ingredients into the bowl of dry ingredients and stir just until everything is moist. Avoid over stirring. It’s okay if there are a few lumps.
Pour the batter into the prepared dish and bake for about 20 minutes, or until the top and edges are golden brown. Cut into 8 pieces and serve.

items.name: Chicken and Rice Soup
ingredients: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken breast (about 2 breast halves)
½ teaspoon red pepper flakes or 1 teaspoon Aleppo pepper
2 green onions, chopped (whites and green parts)
steps: Cook the vegetables. In a large Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium. When the oil shimmers, add the onion, celery, carrots, and garlic. Season with a good pinch of salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the veggies have softened, about 5 minutes.

Poach the chicken. Add the chicken, chicken stock, and water. Season with the oregano, thyme, bay leaf, red pepper flakes, and another dash of salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat to medium-low. Cook until the chicken is nearly fully cooked, 10 to 15 minutes, spooning out any foam that bubbles to the top of the cooking liquid.

Cook the rice. Transfer the chicken to a rimmed plate for now. Add the rinsed rice to the pot and raise the heat to bring the liquid back to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer until the rice is tender, 12 to 15 minutes or so.

Shred the chicken. While the rice is cooking, shred the chicken breasts into smaller pieces using two forks (hold one fork in each hand, tines facing down. Use one fork to pin the chicken in place, then drag the other fork through the meat, pulling away from the first.)

Finish and serve. Add the shredded chicken to the pot and simmer briefly, just to warm the chicken through. Remove and discard the bay leaf. Turn the heat off and stir in the lemon juice and zest, green onion, and fresh parsley. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Ladle into bowls and serve with lemon slices.

items.name: Chocolate Crinkle Cookies
ingredients: 200g/ 6.5oz dark chocolate chips or discs/melts (US: semi-sweet chocolate) – Note 1
60g (4 tbsp) unsalted butter , melted and cooled
2 large eggs , at room temperature (50 – 55g/2oz each, no larger)
¼ cup white sugar / granulated sugar (or caster sugar / superfine sugar)
¼ cup unsweetened cocoa , sifted (not Dutch processed) – Note 1
1 ½ tsp baking powder (make sure yours is still alive), don’t substitute with baking soda
⅛ tsp cooking salt / kosher salt
¼ cup white sugar / granulated sugar (not caster sugar / superfine, it’s too fine)
¾ cup icing sugar / powdered sugar , no need to sift
steps: Melt chocolate, cool 5 min. Add Wet ingredients, whisk well. Stir in Dry ingredients with wooden spoon. Fridge 30 min. Roll 20 – 22 x 1.5 tbsp balls, roll in sugar then pack on icing sugar thickly – only do what fits on the trays. Bake 13 min 180°C/350°F (160°C fan).
Mix dry ingredients – Whisk the cocoa powder, flour, baking powder and salt together in a medium bowl. Set aside.
Melt chocolate – Place the chocolate in a large heatproof bowl. Microwave in 20-second increments, stirring between each, until melted and smooth. Leave to cool for 5 minutes.

Make cookie dough – Add the butter, eggs, both sugars and vanilla to the melted chocolate. Whisk until thoroughly combined. Add the dry ingredients and mix with a wooden spoon until incorporated. The dough should be very thick but too soft to roll into balls. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to firm up, don't leave it in so long the dough gets hard. (Note 2 for skipping this step.)
Preheat oven to 180°C/350°F (160°C fan-forced). Line 2 baking trays with baking paper/parchment paper.
Prepare coating – Place the sugar in one shallow bowl and the icing sugar in another. Wider bowls make coating easier.

Roll balls – Take the dough out of the fridge. It should be firm enough to roll into soft balls (if not, refrigerate a little longer). Scoop out 1 ½ tablespoons of dough (size 40 cookie scoop) and roll into balls. You should get 20–22 balls.

Coat – Roll a ball lightly in the sugar, then coat in the icing sugar, packing it on thickly until the ball is completely covered. Aim for full coverage so you can't see cookie dough! Place on a prepared tray. Repeat with enough balls to fill both trays, spacing them 7.5cm/3" apart.

(I do 6 per tray for the first batch, then 4 – 5 per tray for the second. Feel free to fit more if you have larger trays and oven.) Keep the remaining uncoated balls in the fridge until needed (don't coat until just before baking, it will sweat off).

Bake for 13 minutes. The cookies will puff up into domes and be very soft. Don't open the oven or rotate the trays during baking – this can cause the cookies to collapse. The cookies are ready when they have a light crust on the outside but they will still be jiggly inside.

Cool – Leave the cookies on the trays for 5 minutes to set a bit (the outside goes crispier and the inside will set like fudge). Then carefully transfer to cooling racks using a spatula, cool for another 5 minutes (avoid touching the icing sugar coating with your fingers).
Coat and bake remaining dough balls. Most people enjoy these a bit warm. But I like them fully cool because they become chewier and fudgier!

items.name: Holiday Salad with Cider Vinaigrette
ingredients: Half of a large apple, cut very very thinly on a mandoline
½ cup candied walnuts, cut into small pieces
⅔ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese
steps: Make Dressing: Whisk dressing ingredients or shake in a jar.
Combine Salad Ingredients: Add all salad ingredients to a large bowl (I like to set aside a bit of Parmesan, apple, and candied nuts for topping).
Dress Salad: Just before serving, add dressing to everything, and toss to combine. (Start with a little dressing, then toss, then add a bit more until you feel like you have enough.)
Finish: Garnish with the remaining Parmesan, apple, and candied nuts on top. Fan the apples out in small clusters to make it look pretty 🙂

items.name: 23 Healthy Breakfasts That'll Keep You Full Till Lunch
Maple Pumpkin Overnight Oats
ingredients: 2 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt
¼ cup pure maple syrup; plus more for serving (optional)
½ tsp. ground cinnamon or cardamom; plus more for serving (optional)
Plain whole-milk yogurt, unsalted roasted pumpkin seeds (pepitas), and/or granola (for serving; optional)
steps: Whisk one 15-oz. can pure pumpkin purée, 1½ cups unsweetened milk of choice, 2 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, ¼ cup pure maple syrup, and ½ tsp. ground cinnamon or cardamom in a large bowl until smooth. Add 3 Tbsp.

chia seeds and whisk to combine. Let sit 10 minutes. (Doing this gives the seeds a head start on hydrating and prevents them from sticking together. But if you can’t spare the time, just give the mixture a good stir before serving.)
Stir chia mixture again, then add 1¼ cups old-fashioned oats and mix well to combine. Cover oat mixture and chill at least 8 hours.

Spoon oat mixture into bowls and top with plain whole-milk yogurt, unsalted roasted pumpkin seeds (pepitas), and/or granola, maple syrup, and cinnamon as desired. Do Ahead: Oat mixture (without toppings) can be made 4 days ahead. Keep chilled.

items.name: Pecan Cream Pie With Brown Sugar Custard
ingredients: 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces
10 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick
Rice flour or all-purpose flour (for dusting)
⅔ cup (packed; 133 g) dark brown sugar
¾ cup (packed; 150 g) dark brown sugar
½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
6 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, cut into pieces
steps: Whisk 1⅔ cups (208 g) all-purpose flour, ¼ tsp. baking powder, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Add 2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces; rub into dry ingredients with your fingers until combined (mixture will be very shaggy). Add 10 Tbsp.
chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat, then smash into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea size). Make a well in the center; pour in ¼ cup ice water.
Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute, then knead dough in bowl a couple of times to bring together (some dry bits may remain).

Turn dough out onto a lightly dusted surface; dust top of dough with rice flour or all-purpose flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again. Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting with more flour as needed. Pat into a ½"-thick disk; wrap in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours.

Place racks in upper and lower thirds of oven; preheat to 425°. Let dough sit at room temperature 5 minutes. Unwrap and roll out on a lightly floured surface to a ¼"–⅛"-thick round. Wrap around rolling pin; transfer to a standard 9"-diameter pie dish (preferably metal).

Unfurl into dish, then lift edges and allow dough to slump down into dish. Trim overhang to 1". Fold overhang under and crimp edges as desired. Prick bottom and sides of dough in several places with a fork. Freeze 15 minutes.

Crumple up 2 sheets of parchment paper; smooth out and place over dough. Fill dish with pie weights or dried beans. Set pan on a foil-lined baking sheet and bake crust on lower rack, tenting edges with foil if browning too quickly, until edges are golden brown and bottom is opaque, 35–40 minutes. Remove from oven; reduce oven temperature to 350°. Lift parchment and weights out of pan.

While the crust is baking, whisk 2 large eggs, ⅔ cup (packed; 133 g) dark brown sugar, and remaining 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl. Set egg mixture aside to use for the candied pecan topping and the pie filling.

Melt remaining 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a medium saucepan set over medium. Add 2½ cups (300 g) raw pecans and cook, stirring gently, until nuts are slightly darkened in color and fragrant, 5–7 minutes. Pour through a fine-mesh sieve set over a small bowl, reserving both the pecans and the browned butter. (You’ll use the same pan to make the custard; no need to wash it.)

Transfer ½ cup toasted pecans to another small bowl to make the topping: Add 1 Tbsp. reserved egg mixture and toss to coat. Spread on a parchment-lined baking sheet and bake on upper rack until dry to the touch and a honeycomb-like texture appears on surface, about 5 minutes. Let candied nuts cool.
For the filling: Finely chop remaining toasted pecans and add to the remaining egg mixture along with the reserved browned butter, 2 Tbsp. sour cream, and 1 tsp. vanilla extract. Stir to combine.

Scrape into crust and bake on lower rack until pecan layer is mostly set but still jiggles slightly in the center when gently shaken, 15–18 minutes. Transfer pan to a wire rack; let cool until barely warm, at least 30 minutes.
Do Ahead: Candied pecan topping can be made 3 days ahead; store airtight at room temperature. Crust with pecan layer can be baked 1 day ahead; store, covered with foil, at room temperature.
Heat 1½ cups heavy cream and 1 cup whole milk in the same saucepan you used for the nuts over medium until steaming, about 2 minutes.

Meanwhile, whisk 6 large egg yolks, ¾ cup (packed; 150 g) dark brown sugar, ⅓ cup (40 g) cornstarch, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining ½ cup whole milk in a medium bowl.

Gradually pour warm cream mixture into egg mixture, whisking constantly until combined. Pour mixture back into pan and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it starts to bubble, then becomes glossy and thick (like pudding), 3–4 minutes. Scrape into a medium bowl, add 6 Tbsp.

chilled unsalted butter, cut into pieces, and 4 tsp. vanilla extract, and whisk until butter is melted and custard is emulsified. Cover with plastic wrap, pressing directly onto surface. Let custard stand at room temperature while the pecan layer cools.
The pecan layer can still be slightly warm when you add the custard; neither needs to cool completely.
Uncover custard; whisk until smooth. Spoon over gooey pecan layer, spreading evenly to edges. Cover and chill at least 4 hours and up to 1 day.

Whisk ¼ cup sour cream, 3 Tbsp. powdered sugar, remaining 1 tsp. vanilla extract, a pinch of kosher salt, and remaining 1 cup heavy cream in a medium bowl to medium peaks. Spoon over custard and spread into an even layer. Break candied pecans into large pieces and scatter on top.

Do Ahead: Pie can be assembled 1 day ahead. Chill. Editor’s note: Originally published in October 2025, this recipe has been updated to clarify the recommended pan size and instructions. The ingredients and tested techniques remain unchanged.

items.name: 19 Pumpkin Purée Recipes From Cake to Pie
Thanksgiving Chicken and Gravy
ingredients: 2 teaspoons fresh thyme ( or rosemary, chopped )
2 ¼ teaspoons Diamond Crystal kosher salt (use less with Mortons, plus more to taste)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (plus more to taste)
3 tablespoons all-purpose flour (or gluten-free flour alternative)
2 cups chicken broth (or stock, or turkey stock)
steps: In a small bowl, stir together the thyme, sage, dried oregano, and the olive oil. Remove the neck and giblets and reserve for stock, if using. Loosen the skin around the shoulders of the bird and around the cavity.
Carefully slide your hands underneath the skin to loosen it from the breast, thighs, and drumsticks. Rub the herb and oil mixture on the meat and under the skin then pat the skin back into place.

In a second small bowl, stir together the salt, sugar, and black pepper. Rub the seasoning inside the cavity and on to the skin. Place the chicken onto a wire rack set inside of a rimmed baking sheet and refrigerate the chicken, uncovered, overnight or a few hours if you want to cook it the same day.

Remove from the refrigerator and spritz the skin on all sides of the chicken with olive oil spray. Tuck the wing tips behind the neck, tie the legs together with kitchen twine, and let the chicken temper on the counter for 20 minutes.
Position a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 425°F. If using a probe, insert the thermometer in the thickest part of the breast (not touching the bone) and set the temperature to160F.

Roast until the breast reaches 160°F and the thighs reach at least 175°F or higher (they’ll rise slightly as the chicken rests), 45 to 55 minutes, or longer depending on the size of the chicken. Rotate the baking sheet front to back after 25 minutes.

Carefully transfer the chicken, still on the wire rack, to a cutting board. Let rest for 15 minutes before carving, allowing the juices to redistribute and the residual heat to bring the breast temperature to 165°F.

As the chicken is resting, pour the fat and juices from the baking sheet into a small bowl. Add 2 tablespoons of the reserved fat and juices (discard the rest) into a small saucepan and warm over medium heat. Sprinkle the flour over the fat, stir to combine, and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.

Whisk in the broth and bring the mixture to a simmer, 2 to 4 minutes. Continue to whisk and cook until thickened to a creamy gravy, about 5 additional minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve alongside the carved roasted chicken.

items.name: Baked Mac and Cheese
ingredients: ¼ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
¾ tsp salt or to taste,
8 oz. sharp cheddar freshly grated & divided, (2 cups) $1.87**
4 oz Colby Jack freshly grated & divided, (1 cup) $0.94**
1 Tbsp salted butter for the cooked pasta,
⅛ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
1 oz sharp cheddar freshly grated, (¼ cup) $0.23**
steps: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 2-quart baking dish.
Shred the cheddar and Colby Jack using the large holes of a box grater. Microwave the milk for 1-2 minutes, until warm but not hot.***

Bring the water and bouillon to a boil in a large pot. Add the macaroni and cook for 6 minutes, or until slightly underdone. Drain in a colander, add 1 tablespoon of butter, and toss until melted. Set aside while you prepare the sauce.****
In a small bowl, combine the panko, melted butter, garlic powder, smoked paprika, black pepper, and grated cheddar for the topping. Mix until the breadcrumbs are evenly coated.
Melt ¼ cup butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for about 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture is pale blond and slightly nutty.
Gradually whisk in the warm milk, adding a splash at a time and whisking until smooth before each addition. Stir in the dry mustard, garlic powder, smoked paprika, black pepper, and salt.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes, whisking frequently and scraping the corners of the pan, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

Remove the pan from the heat and let the sauce cool for about 1 minute. Add the cheddar and Colby Jack a handful at a time, stirring until melted before adding more. Reserve ½ cup of the combined cheese for layering in the casserole. If the sauce becomes too thick to stir easily, whisk in a splash of milk.*****
Fold the cooked macaroni into the cheese sauce until evenly coated.
Spread half of the macaroni mixture into the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle the reserved ½ cup of cheese evenly over the top.
Add the remaining macaroni mixture and spread it evenly. Sprinkle the breadcrumb topping over the surface without pressing it down.

Bake for about 25 minutes, until the edges are bubbling and the topping is golden. If the topping needs more color, broil for about 1 minute, watching closely to prevent burning. Let the mac and cheese rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.name: Creamy Stovetop Mac and Cheese
ingredients: 4 cups freshly shredded cheese (15 ounces, or two blocks – I use mild cheddar and Gruyere)
½ cup to ¾ cup warm water at the end
steps: Grate Your Cheese: This recipe works best if you grate your own cheese!

Cook Noodles: Cook the elbow macaroni according to package directions, with a generous pinch of salt added to the water. Drain, set aside, and drizzle with a bit of oil to prevent noodles from sticking.

Butter and Flour: In a large skillet or Dutch oven, melt the butter over medium low heat. Add flour; whisk to incorporate. Let it bubble for 2-3 minutes to cook out any floury taste. Add onion powder and salt.
Add Milk: Slowly add the milk, ½ cup at a time. It’ll start out clumpy, but as you whisk and add more liquid, it will turn into a smooth and thickened sauce.
Add Cream: Add heavy cream; simmer and whisk until the sauce is smooth and lightly thickened. Turn the heat off. (You want it to be warm enough to melt the cheese, but not boiling hot.)
Add Cheese: Add the grated cheese to the warm sauce. Stir to melt completely. (If it’s not melting smoothly, put it back on low heat).
Finish: Add your noodles. Stir to coat. It’ll be cheesy and delicious. This is where you’ll add warm water, a little bit at a time, to reach your desired final consistency. Serve immediately!

items.name: Dukkah recipe
ingredients: 1 ½ tbsp blanched almonds (ie skinless almonds), substitute skin-on (Note 2)
¼ heaped teaspoon cooking salt / kosher salt (halve for table salt, + 50% for flakes) – Note 3
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C/350°F (160°C fan-forced).
Roast nuts – Spread the hazelnuts, almonds and pistachios on a tray. Bake for 5 minutes.
Roast seeds – Add sesame seeds and fennel seeds to the tray. Shake the tray to spread evenly. Bake for 3 minutes.

Coarsely blitz – Cool on the tray for 15 minutes. Pour everything into a mini food processor. Add the Spices. Blitz until coarsely ground – don't let it become a powder. (Or do this in a mortar and pestle, or in a ziplock bag and bash using a rolling pin or meat mallet).
Note – the chunkier nut bits will rise to the surface and powder will sink, so don't be tricked into thinking it's chunkier than it is!
Use as a bread dipper with olive oil or sprinkling over "everything"! Use generously, not a sparse sprinkle, defeats the purpose!

As a bread dip (traditional) – Pour dukkah into a small shallow bowl and a good extra virgin olive oil in another (my favourite shop-bought is Lomondo from Mudgee in NSW). Pile warm cubes of bread, focaccia or wedges of pita bread on the side. Dip bread into olive oil first then the dukkah (it will stick to the oil). Eat!
Dukkah bread – Brush bread with olive oil then sprinkle with dukkah and sea salt flakes. Ideal to use bread with a large surface area (eg pita bread, Lebanese bread, focaccia)
Crumbing – Add to a breadcrumb mixture, like these Crumbed Baked Chicken Tenders or Schnitzel!

*Note on cooking* If using dukkah to sprinkle on things that go into the oven, be mindful of the nuts burning. Best to use for things that have a short bake time (eg on bread, ~10 min in oven) or mix it with breadcrumbs. Otherwise, use to sprinkle on the cooked food.
Topping or finish – Sprinkle generously over foods to make a good dish gourmet, or to make simple foods instantly more exciting!
Examples: Garlic prawns, roasted vegetables, glazed carrots, oven baked chicken breast, a store bought roast chicken (add olive oil as well), pan fried fish, avocado toast, scrambled eggs.
It'd be spectacular sprinkled on these Sweet Potato Steaks or Maple Roasted Carrots with Whipped Tahini (instead of pine nuts). (Remember – use generously!)
Garnish for dips – like hummus, whipped feta and labne.

items.name: Sausage Stuffing Recipe
ingredients: 10 Tbsp. unsalted butter, divided, plus more for dish
1 (1–1¼-lb.) loaf country-style white bread, torn into 1" pieces
1 lb. breakfast sausage, casings removed if needed
1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt
3 cups low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth, divided
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 350°. Grease a 13x9" baking dish with unsalted butter. Arrange one 1–1¼-lb. loaf country-style white bread, torn into 1" pieces, in a single layer on a large rimmed baking sheet and bake until dried out and golden around the edges, 30–40 minutes. Let cool.

Meanwhile, melt 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high heat. Cook 1 lb. breakfast sausage, casings removed if needed, stirring and breaking into small pieces, until well browned and cooked through, 8–10 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer sausage to a small plate, leaving fat behind.

Reduce dial to medium heat and add remaining 8 Tbsp. unsalted butter to fat in pot; heat until melted. Cook 2 medium onions, finely chopped, 6 celery stalks, finely chopped, 8 garlic cloves, coarsely chopped, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp.

fennel seeds (if using), stirring occasionally, until onions are softened and golden around the edges, 12–15 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth along with sausage, ½ cup (packed) coarsely chopped parsley, 2 Tbsp. finely chopped sage, 2 Tbsp.
finely chopped thyme, and ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper.

Whisk 3 large eggs and remaining 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth in a small bowl to combine, then stir into pot (don’t worry, eggs won’t scramble). Add bread to pot and toss gently to combine. Let sit, tossing occasionally, until liquid is almost completely absorbed, about 10 minutes.

Transfer stuffing to prepared dish (don’t pack or press down) and cover loosely with foil. Place dish on a clean large rimmed baking sheet and bake until stuffing is hot throughout (an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should register 160°), 35–45 minutes.

Increase oven temperature to 400° and remove foil (no need to remove stuffing from oven while heat increases). Continue to bake until stuffing is light golden brown on top, 25–30 minutes longer. Do Ahead: Bread can be baked 1 day ahead; store loosely covered at room temperature.

Stuffing can be assembled 1 day ahead; cover and chill. Bring to room temperature before baking. Editor’s note: This sausage stuffing recipe was first printed in our November 2023 issue; it has been updated for style. Head this way for more of our favorite Thanksgiving side dishes →

items.name: Hot Honey Brussels Sprouts
ingredients: 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided, plus more
⅓ cup sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar
¾ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes
3 scallions, thinly sliced on a diagonal
steps: Place a rimmed baking sheet on bottom rack of oven; preheat to 450°. Toss 1½ lb. brussels sprouts, trimmed, halved, and ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil in a large bowl; sprinkle with ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and season with freshly ground black pepper.
Carefully remove baking sheet from oven. Using tongs, arrange brussels sprouts cut-side down on hot baking sheet. Roast brussels on bottom rack until softened and deeply browned, 15–25 minutes.

Meanwhile, bring ¼ cup honey to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring often, until honey is a deep amber color but not burnt (it will be foamy, that’s okay), 3–4 minutes.

Remove from heat and add ⅓ cup sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar (it will bubble up quite aggressively) and ¾ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes; whisk until sauce is smooth. Return saucepan to medium heat and add 3 Tbsp. unsalted butter and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt. Cook, whisking constantly, until glaze is glossy, bubbling, and slightly thickened, 3–4 minutes.

Transfer roasted brussels sprouts to a large bowl. Add half the hot honey glaze and scallions and toss to combine. Taste and add more glaze if desired. Transfer to a platter and top with lemon zest. Serve remaining glaze alongside.

Do ahead: Glaze can be made 5 days ahead; refrigerate after cooling. Editor’s note: This recipe was first published in September 2018 as “Charred Brussels Sprouts With Warm Honey Glaze”; it has been updated for style and clarity. Head this way for more of our best Thanksgiving side dishes →

items.name: 37 Family Dinner Ideas You’ll Make on Repeat
French Onion Chicken
ingredients: ½ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
steps: Gather and prepare all ingredients. Slice the chicken breasts in half, lengthwise.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat. Pat the chicken dry with paper towels. Then season them evenly with ½ teaspoon of salt and pepper.

Once the pan is hot, gently place the chicken in the pan. Do not overcrowd and work in batches if necessary. Let the chicken cook undisturbed for 4-5 minutes on each side until a golden-brown crust forms. Ensure the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 165°F. Cook longer if necessary.
